sourceCoverage.note: Six issuer originals read; vendor tests are attributed and exploratory statuses retained.
Issuer-specific exchange completeness remains unresolved; fresh entrypoint probes are a separate evidence artifact, not a no-change verdict.
No new earnings or earnings-call figures are used in this release.
No permit, energization or capacity allocation is asserted. AEMA is an industry initiative.
The afternoon ERCOT/PJM content is preserved; no complete additional government review was achieved tonight.
MLPerf data is reported as NVIDIA's preview submission; no independent reproduction or new binding standard is claimed.
Read issuer descriptions of AEMA, China Mobile joint validation, AirTrunk's MoU and Lambda's test; independent counterpart confirmation is not implied.
DCD original pages for Serverfarm, Schneider and Goodman returned access failures; headline-only discoveries are held, not republished.

change.description: Read NVIDIA's MLPerf 6.1 preview article: Rubin NVL72 reports Qwen3-VL up to 3.7x and DeepSeek-R1 up to 2.5x GB300 NVL72. Preview category and software/scenario dependence retained; no availability or revenue claim inferred.

impact.consequence: The comparison shifts attention to rack-level throughput and software integration. Procurement still needs latency targets, power use, pricing and actual delivery availability.

change.description: Read NVIDIA's AEMA launch article. Emerald AI, Google and NVIDIA propose performance-based load flexibility, response metrics and interconnection pathways; this is industry advocacy, not enacted regulation or approved MW.

impact.consequence: Interconnection competition may increasingly depend on demonstrable load flexibility, not just requested power. Faster access remains a policy objective rather than an approved project outcome.

change.description: Read SK hynix's FACT response to September 16 reporting. The company says neither Ohio leasing nor an Intel/cloud-company venture is decided. Do not change 'not finalized' into a categorical denial of discussions.

impact.consequence: A potential arrangement would matter for US memory supply, but it cannot yet be counted as capacity or a completed venture. The response addresses decision status, not a denial of all talks.

change.description: Read AirTrunk's September 15 MoU announcement. Cryogenic cooling and quantum-ready infrastructure are exploratory with techno-economic evaluation. The source does not establish a commercial facility or achieved savings.

impact.consequence: Cooling research is moving beyond conventional liquid cooling. Deployment economics depend on whether computing gains outweigh refrigeration power, equipment costs and operating complexity.

change.description: Read NVIDIA's September 15 AI Infra Summit article. Lambda validation fits 19 Blackwell nodes into the budget normally serving 16 at full power, with about 24% higher token output and 23% performance-per-watt gain. Customer-specific test, not a universal fleet result.

impact.consequence: Power-constrained facilities may raise output through scheduling and power management, not only new electrical capacity. Workload type, performance targets and power variation remain critical trade-offs.
